title: Azhar Kerrash
_note: PRO_06: the Guest. He never raises his voice. Lines keep MAIN_QUEST.md IDs where they have one, for voicing. Options show short text; spoken is the fuller line he says. starts: the first whose condition holds opens the conversation.

start.speaker: The stranger
start.text: [Warm, rueful, taking his hat off.] Forgive the intrusion. Hot day, long road. A man heard there was a farm on this hill with the best goat cheese on the coast.

choices.spoken: The cheese isn't for sale today.

neighbour.speaker: The stranger
neighbour.text: Just a neighbour. A big neighbour. [He sits anyway.]

free.speaker: The stranger
free.text: [He laughs.] Then I'll eat it for free and call it generosity. [He sits.]

bread.speaker: The stranger
bread.text: [To Nadira.] Where did you learn bread like this? You don't hear a Forebear accent from those hills.

aunt.speaker: Nadira
aunt.text: My aunt. She was particular about bread.

tavi.speaker: The stranger
tavi.text: [He ruffles Tavi's hair.] And who is this? Tavi. A good name, a sea name. [He reaches down to the dog and scratches the torn ear, very gently.] And this one's a fighter, I see.

war.speaker: The stranger
war.text: [Curious, pleasant.] You've a soldier's back. Hegathe, was it? The relief column?

choices.spoken: Conscript. Three years. I don't talk about it.
I farm goats. That's my war.

gently.speaker: The stranger
gently.text: Everything on this coast is my business. Gently.

salt.speaker: The stranger
salt.text: [He takes a pinch of salt from the pot and sets it on the table, a little white mound. Kind, almost sad.] Now. The Patriot's Share. I do hate this part. Twenty sacks a season, for the protection of this whole coast. Your neighbours were late. You've been so good about it.

choices.text: [Speech 25] We have no sacks to spare.
choices.spoken: We grow goats and barley. I haven't got twenty sacks to spare.
You've eaten. Get out of my house.
We'll find it. Give us time.

nobody.speaker: The stranger
nobody.text: Nobody ever does. Think it over. I'll come back for the answer.

shame.speaker: The stranger
shame.text: That's two people today who've refused me. Shame. [Outside, his men shift.]

pleased.speaker: The stranger
pleased.text: [He is pleased.] There. That wasn't so hard. Hardly anything is, if people are reasonable.

judge.speaker: The stranger
judge.text: [The room is very quiet. Dune growls.] He's a good judge of character.

look.speaker: The stranger
look.text: [He looks at Nadira too long. She drops a spoon.] You have the look of someone I knew.

face.speaker: Nadira
face.text: [Steady. Too steady.] I get that a lot. I have one of those faces.

come.speaker: The stranger
come.text: [Smiling.] No. It'll come to me. [He stands, and puts his hat back on.] Thank you for the bread.
